_comment: POST-B2 proposal-seam tasks. Each one is a CASE, not a prompt: bench/propose.py builds a real
careloop.state.Case from it and drives careloop.agents.planner.PlannerAgent.propose, so what is
measured is the seam CareLoop actually ships -- planner_system_prompt(), planner_user_prompt(),
the closed propose_* schemas, tool_choice any, and the one bounded retry.
This is a STRUCTURAL benchmark. It asks whether the provider can form a proposal against these
schemas at all, which of the four failure types occur, and whether the retry recovers one. It
is deliberately NOT a correctness benchmark: `expects` is filled only where a single tool is
the unambiguous next action, and is null everywhere the case genuinely admits several. Reading
the null rows as errors would be inventing a rubric after the fact.
The four replan tasks carry prior_denials, which is the state no earlier benchmark reached: a
single call from a clean context cannot produce it, and docs/model-benchmark.md lists it as
gap 5 -- 'the single most important behaviour in the system and it is entirely unmeasured'.
Facts are written at the trust level the case would really hold them at. The planner never sees
a trust level (invariant 6), so this changes no prompt; it is here so the fixture cannot drift
into describing a case the graph could not produce.
